angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 548,907 km at 154.54 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.4709 +/- 0.0286 mas (same row, RUWE 1.54): 154.54 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.789 +/- 0.025 solar radii from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-182 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract): 548,907 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.823 +/- 0.036 solar masses from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-182 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5128 +/- 79 K from Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-182 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Thygesen et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-182 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....165..155T/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-182.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.559, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
